subject: Post-discovery: lock sizing deep-dive window & MAP handoff
messages:
From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: emily.santos@nebulapay.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-discovery recap + request to schedule sizing deep-dive

Hi Emily — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a couple of proposed next steps so we can lock in the sizing deep-dive with the right folks.

Key notes from the call:
- Primary workload: near-real-time payments enrichment (tokenization + risk scoring) behind API gateway
- Target latency goal: p95 <= 120ms for single-request flows, occasional batched jobs for reconciliation with higher latency tolerance
- Expected steady-state QPS: ~60 qps with short bursts to 250 qps during batch windows
- Data residency: US-only; no customer PII persists in our cache, but audit logs required

Next steps I propose:
1) 60-minute technical sizing deep-dive (we'll bring an infra engineer and a runtime specialist)
2) Please confirm the throughput profile & any spike windows (attach load profile if you have one)
3) Share any security/compliance constraints we should pre-load for the call (SOC 2 artifacts, session recording rules)

Proposed windows (all PDT):
- Tue Apr 20, 10:00–11:00
- Wed Apr 21, 14:00–15:00
- Thu Apr 22, 09:00–10:00

If those don't work, tell me two 60-minute slots that do and I will loop in Marcus (infra) and Ben (solutions). I attached a draft mutual-action-plan (MAP-draft.pdf) so we can align responsibilities pre-call.

Thanks — want to make this run efficiently.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
attachments: MAP-draft.pdf (application/pdf, stub)

From: Emily Santos <emily.santos@nebulapay.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: tom.reed@nebulapay.com
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 09:28:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-discovery recap + request to schedule sizing deep-dive

Jonas — appreciate the clear recap. Tom and I reviewed internally and the notes match our expectations. A few clarifications and our availability below.

Throughput and profile (preliminary):
- Steady: 50–70 qps (mostly 1–2 token request flows)
- Day-of-batch spikes: ~200–250 qps for 5–7 minutes (evening settlement window)
- Large reconciliation job runs nightly (15–30 minutes) at ~400 qps but high latency acceptable there

Latency SLO: p95 120ms is our target for the API path. For batch jobs we can tolerate up to 3s.

Security: we can upload a short load profile CSV and the SOC questionnaire. Uploading the load profile now; will share SOC artifacts after legal approves.

Availability (PDT):
- Tue Apr 20: 10:00 OK for Tom
- Wed Apr 21: 14:00 also works if you need more time for Marcus to join

We prefer Tue 10:00 if you can make it. I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm the exact attendee list.

Thanks,
Emily Santos
Senior Engineering Manager
NebulaPay
attachments: nebulanet_load_profile.csv (text/csv, stub)

Pre-call asks for a productive session:
- If you can, attach the CSV or paste a short example of a 1-minute sample (we'll use it to tune batching profiles)
- Confirm whether encrypted-at-rest KMS is required for the test environment (yes/no)
- Share any IPs for whitelist if you want us to pre-configure network routing

I've created a short MAP draft and added a placeholder row for the call (link below) — please feel free to add attendees and accept the row for owner assignments. I'll follow up with a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Agenda (30/20/10):
- 30m: workload profile & runbook for steady-state + spikes
- 20m: runtime architecture & quantization/batching knobs for cost control
- 10m: action items, MAP owners, and procurement checklist

Link to MAP: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1NeBuLa-Map/edit

I'll send the calendar invite in the next 30 minutes.

Jonas
